items.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021
items.q: Woody’s band, Chuck’s band — Chuck Mangione’s band, Bill Evans, and all the different sidemen— all the different leaders that I worked for in New York

ctx.x: Were the people you played, the leaders, would they tell you, would they give you guidance, would they like chew you out or was it sort of like, apparently Count Basie wouldn’t say anything unless he was really unhappy. So I’m just wondering, did you ever be — like look for guidance or almost welcome it and not get it?

I don’t know that I ever actually asked anybody, but I was fortunate in that Woody’s band, Chuck’s band — Chuck Mangione’s band, Bill Evans, and all the different sidemen— all the different leaders that I worked for in New York, they really hired you for you, so they allowed you to learn or they allowed your input. They wanted you to interpret the music the way you heard it.

I love the music of Chuck Mangione and I actually — full disclosure, I asked Gap, I said, “Well what are some things I should know about Joe?” And he said nice things, rest assured. He sent me a link to a really nice video of the group when you were in it, 1980 Live at Monterey, and there’s a full tune on there, it’s fairly lengthy. And you have an extended drum solo on it, and I noticed that you started just on the snare drum and you started this pretty like intricate rhythm, and then you picked it up and you…
